title: Easy Problems
description: Basic greedy problems to build up logical thinking.
identify: Problems where making a locally optimal choice leads to a globally optimal solution
explanation: Greedy algorithms make the optimal choice at each step as they attempt to find the overall optimal way to solve the entire problem. Sorting the input is often the key first step.

title: Medium Problems
description: More complex greedy algorithms involving scheduling, intervals, and optimizations.
explanation: These problems require sorting the data based on a specific criteria (like ending time for meetings, or starting time for intervals) and then greedily picking the best available options or merging them.

title: Hard Problems
description: Advanced greedy algorithms that often require careful tracking of state or multiple passes.
explanation: These problems often involve greedily extending a 'reach' boundary or using multiple passes (like left-to-right and right-to-left) to satisfy constraints optimally.
